prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows a paved road stretching forward from the foreground into the dark upper background, flanked by raised grassy banks on the right (1.5–3 m away) and three walking companions entering from the left edge. Across the five frames, as the camera wearer turns and looks slightly up and left, a person in a blue jacket enters the lower-left foreground within arm's reach (0.5–1 m away, brightest white), positioned to the left of and slightly behind a person in a yellow hoodie (1–1.8 m away, light grey), who in turn walks about 0.5–1 m behind and to the left of a person in a dark blue shirt (2–3 m away, mid-grey). All three companions are spaced roughly 0.5–1 m apart, facing and moving forward-right along the road with their heads oriented ahead rather than toward the camera wearer, while the nearer companions progressively occlude the lower bodies of those further ahead. The depth map makes the stepped front-to-back distance ordering of the three overlapping companions and the road's continuous ground-plane gradient much clearer than the RGB image alone. However, it is unreliable for small ground objects like the white container on the right grass in frame 1 (around 2 m away) and the two distant pedestrians 15–25 m ahead on the road in frames 2–3, which vanish into the smooth background gradient.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map isolates the people along the left side of the road from the unlabelled asphalt and vegetation background, tracking their rightward and upward shift into the frame as the camera wearer turns toward them. It captures the three nearby companions walking forward-right in a staggered group—the closest person in blue (0.5–1 m, within arm's reach of the wearer and the middle person), the middle person in yellow (1–1.8 m, within arm's reach of both neighbours), and the farthest person in a dark shirt (2–3 m)—all facing ahead along the road and looking away from the camera wearer. In frame 3, the map uniquely detects the two tiny pedestrians walking 15–25 m ahead near the top edge of the road, which are very hard to spot in the RGB strip and completely absent from the other maps. However, the segmentation is unreliable in several places: in frame 1 it misclassifies the yellow-hoodied person's lower leg and the road's yellow line as a 'skateboard', in frames 1–3 the closest person in blue at the bottom-left corner is either missed or merged into the middle person's mask, and in frame 5 the closest person's mask splits into two separate horizontal colour regions while the middle person in yellow is mostly absorbed into the foreground mask due to heavy occlusion.
descriptions.pose: The pose map renders a 2D yellow body skeleton on a black background only for the farthest of the three nearby companions (the person in the dark shirt, roughly 2–3 m to the left and in front of the camera wearer) during frames 3 to 5, with no magenta hand keypoints detected in any frame. The skeleton's right-profile alignment of head, shoulder, hip, knee, and ankle keypoints shows this person facing and walking forward-right along the road, looking ahead rather than toward the camera wearer, with their arms hanging down within reach of their own torso and hips. Across frames 3 to 5, the skeleton shifts higher and slightly rightward in the image as the camera tilts up and left, while in frames 4 and 5 it estimates the positions of the lower legs and feet even where they are partly occluded by the nearer person in yellow—a spatial detail hidden in the RGB image. However, the pose map is highly unreliable across the sequence: it completely fails to detect the dark-shirted person in frames 1 and 2 when their head and upper torso are partly out of view at the left edge, and it misses the two closer, heavily overlapping companions in the yellow and blue tops (at 0.5–1.8 m) as well as the distant pedestrians in every frame.
